claims.text: The starting material is an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a uniform, fine lamellar structure.
Laser surface shock peening will introduce high-intensity compressive residual stresses.
Laser surface shock peening will refine the near-surface microstructure.
Repeated laser shock peening passes will be applied at room temperature using water confinement.
Energy density and pulse frequency can be optimized to maximize compressive residual stress without damaging the underlying lamellar structure.
The treatment will create a robust near-surface layer with high compressive residual stress.
The treated near-surface layer will have a refined microstructure.
The treated near-surface layer will have minimized defect density.
Compressive residual stresses will retard crack initiation under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading.
Compressive residual stresses will retard crack propagation under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading.
The refined surface microstructure will decrease the corrosion rate.
The refined surface microstructure will mitigate room-temperature creep.
Laser surface shock peening will improve the surface stress distribution relevant to fastener durability.
Treated fasteners will have longer fatigue life than untreated fasteners.
Treated fasteners will have lower room-temperature creep rates than untreated fasteners.
Treated fasteners will have greater corrosion resistance than untreated fasteners.
The treatment will improve overall mechanical performance and operational reliability under extreme conditions.
The as-cast fine-lamellar alloy currently falls below industrial performance requirements for fasteners in severe environments.
The intervention is applicable under extreme temperature variations, long-term static and cyclic loading, and exposure to corrosive media.
The intervention remains applicable only if processing does not alter the bulk lamellar structure.
